text.p: Lehman Bros Holdings Inc said President T. Christopher Pettit has resigned and the company will not name a replacement for Pettit.
A company spokesman was not available for comment on why Pettit resigned.

In a statement, Lehman said Pettit, 51, was named president and a director in 1994 after having managed day-to-day activities of the Lehman Brothers division of Shearson Lehman Brothers since 1991. He also served as chief operating officer until earlier this year, when he set aside his operating responsibilities to spearhead a newly established senior client contact effort for the company.
Analysts said Petitt's resignation is not completely surprising, adding the fact that Lehman will not name a replacement fits its senior management restructuring of earlier this year.
In April, Petitt relinquished the added title of chief operating officer to spearhead a "major client contact and service effort" designed to enhance revenue generation for the firm.

"It is not that surprising," said one analyst. "The firm had gone through the reorganization and there has been a whole shift in management. Chris took on a lesser role and he may have decided to go do something different."
Petitt has also resigned from Lehman Brothers' board of directors.
